question: Should Slack preserve separate tool-progress delivery when preview aggregation is disabled, and should the new progress-intent metadata become a permanent shared Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The patch changes existing user-visible delivery semantics and creates a cross-plugin API boundary; maintainers must choose the compatibility policy and permanent contract owner before implementation can be finalized.

options.title: Preserve and type progress
options.body: Keep separate progress when configured, add one closed shared contract, and suppress or react only when Slack has another active progress surface.

options.title: Approve universal suppression
options.body: Intentionally suppress transient Codex progress regardless of existing settings, with updated documentation and explicit upgrade proof.

options.title: Move routing upstream
options.body: Remove the Codex-to-Slack metadata seam and make the generic channel progress pipeline own transient delivery classification.

recommendation.title: Preserve and type progress
recommendation.body: Keep separate progress when configured, add one closed shared contract, and suppress or react only when Slack has another active progress surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available cross-surface owner signal for deciding both channel delivery compatibility and the Codex producer boundary.
